title: a tagged template whose tag returns a Result is a Result-producing invocation, so dropping it is a discard — inside a function and at top level alike
notes: specification/failures.mdx:136: 'A Result MUST be treated as a must-use value. A source program MUST NOT silently discard a Result without returning, matching, transforming, inspecting, or unwrapping it.' specification/type-system.mdx:56: 'An ignored Result MUST be a compile error.' A tagged template is an invocation of its tag; if the tag returns a Result, the template expression IS a Result, and an expression statement that is one discards it. WHY THIS CASE EXISTS: the must-consume rule recognized a producer by looking for a call expression, and a tagged template is not one. The whole family — the tag's declared Result, its inferred failure channel, and the obligation the value carries — was invisible at this one spelling. The consequence is the one this rule exists to prevent: the tagged template on line 22 throws, the throw is lifted into the Result the tag declares, and nothing ever looks at it, so the program continues as if the tag had succeeded. FOUR POSITIONS RATHER THAN ONE, and each is a distinct code path: inside a function and at module top level, for both the tagged template AND an ordinary call. The two ordinary calls are the ATTRIBUTION CONTROL — they were already refused, so their presence is what says the two template rows are the new statement and not a symptom of the whole file being rejected. The top-level pair matters separately because the top-level obligation is enforced by a different traversal from the in-function one on both backends, and a fix applied to only one of them leaves half the family open. WHAT THIS CASE DELIBERATELY DOES NOT PIN: the message. `SMITHERS1301` carries one fixed sentence, byte-identical on both backends, that names the remediation and no part of this program. It also does not pin the `panic`-tagged-template spelling (`` panic`x` ``), which is a recorded open question on both backends about whether the compiler-recognized `panic` has a tagged form at all; folding it in would make this case's green depend on a question nobody has answered. VERIFIED LOAD-BEARING, not assumed: mutating the declared line 22 to 21 — one line up, onto the blank line before the first top-level statement, which is where a rule anchoring a top-level obligation at the end of the preceding declaration would report — turns the case red on BOTH backends with the position diff printed, and the file was restored byte-identically (sha256 136604c34d4b4b807c36dec31f0a2602a8ea52931e1865406113a43a93674696 before and after, that digest being this file's content at the moment the mutation ran — the sentence recording it is appended afterwards, so the shipped file necessarily hashes differently). The paired positive control is `a-consumed-result-from-a-tagged-template-is-accepted`, where the same tag's Result is matched on both the success and the failure side and must keep compiling AND RUNNING, so a fix that refuses every tagged template turns that case red instead of passing quietly.
